The maids bowed deeply, apologizing for their lack of attention, which only made Haruna and Yuko look even more guilty.
Their cheeks colored as they waved the apologies off, clearly not wanting the staff to dig any deeper into how the group had actually appeared inside the house.
I kept walking toward the front.
Jayden, Claire, and Yelena fell into step behind me without needing to be told.
"We’ll go wherever you go," Jayden said quietly.
Claire simply nodded.
Yelena’s expression was still a little sulky from earlier, but she followed all the same.
"Okay," I answered.
We stepped outside into the open air.
The moment my feet touched the path, I felt it—a faint flicker of presence on the rooftop of the main building.
I turned my head just in time to catch a brief glimpse of a figure before it vanished from sight.
I spread my telekinesis outward in a sharp, invisible sweep, mapping the area in an instant.
The signature was familiar.
Akane.
She had been watching from the roof, and the second she realized I had noticed her, she had withdrawn.
But not far enough to escape the reach of my senses.
I now knew exactly where she was.

chapters.title: Chapter 1256: Akane’s Conflicting Heart
paragraphs: I turned to Jayden, Claire, and Yelena.
"I changed my mind. You guys wait inside. I have something to check."
They nodded without question and headed back through the entrance. Once they were gone, I looked up toward the rooftop and spoke clearly into the open air.
"You’re already here... why are you hiding?"

There was a brief pause, then a softswishof fabric. Akane dropped down from her vantage point and landed lightly in front of me. She wore a fitted black assassin’s outfit beneath a long black cloak, her face hidden behind a dark mask that left only her sharp eyes visible.
"How are you?" she asked, voice even.
"I’m fine. Were you worried about me?"
Akane’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"No. If someone wants to die by themselves, I figure I cannot save them." The words carried a clear edge of contempt.
I stepped closer.
"Are you still angry about that?"
She turned her head away.
"No. Why would I be angry? Just die all you want. It was Tachibana and Hitomi who were worried about you. So I promised them I would check on you."
She delivered the next part like a prepared statement, each word carefully measured.
"You were not here, so I waited and came each day. Now that you are back and doing well... I will go back."
Her voice was steady, but I could feel the faint tremor underneath it. The moment she shifted her weight to leave, I reached out and caught her wrist.
"Wait, Master Akane."
The title made her stop cold.
"I am not your master."

I pulled her in and wrapped my arms around her, holding her tightly against me. The black cloak and the rigid set of her shoulders didn’t soften, but she didn’t push me away either. Her hands stayed clenched at her sides, fingers digging into her own palms.
Through the contact, I caught the sudden rush of her thoughts.
[He’s hugging me... why is he hugging me so tightly? This is... embarrassing. My heart is beating too fast. He can probably feel it. Damn it... I shouldn’t have let him get this close.]
I held the embrace for a long moment, speaking quietly against the side of her mask.
"I’m sorry for making you so worried. And thank you for coming to see me."
Her thoughts kept spinning.
[He’s apologizing...? I thought he would be angry that I spoke to him like that. I was rude. I snapped at him. He should be angry. Why does it feel worse that he isn’t?]
I finally stepped back, though I kept my hands lightly on her upper arms.
"How are Tachibana and Hitomi doing?"
"They are fine," she answered too quickly. "Hitomi’s and Tachibana’s are... the same as always."
"Are you going on any dangerous mission right now?"
"No. I have not been on any mission since then."
I extended a thin thread of telepathy and caught the thoughts she wasn’t speaking aloud.
[I need to find out who was behind Hitomi’s attack... that seemed premeditated.]
[I can’t let him know, or he’ll follow.]
[If he gets involved again, he might actually die this time. I can’t... I won’t let that happen.]
I looked at her directly.
"You’re lying."
Akane’s eyes widened a fraction behind the mask. Her body tensed.
"I am not lying."
She glanced away almost immediately.
"Look at my eyes when you say that."
She forced her gaze back to mine, but the defiance in her voice only sharpened.
"I have not taken on any mission. I am just investigating. And who are you to question these things?"
The sudden outburst caught me off guard. Akane seemed to realize how sharp she had sounded a second later. Her shoulders stiffened further.
[I did it again... I raised my voice at him. He’s going to be angry for real this time. I keep pushing him away, and then I feel guilty. Why do I always do this?]
"...I am sorry," she said, quieter. "I..."
I let my expression fall, voice quiet and deliberately wounded.
"Yes. You’re right. I am no one."
The words hit her harder than I expected. Her hands curled into tighter fists at her sides, and her voice rose with clear agitation.
"No—that’s not what I meant. I just don’t want to involve you..."
Her thoughts spilled over, raw and conflicted.

[He’s making that face... he thinks I don’t care. That isn’t true. I came here every day. I waited. I was worried. But if I say that, he’ll never stay away when it’s dangerous. I can’t let him follow me into this. I already failed to protect Hitomi once. I won’t fail again by dragging him into it.]
She took a half-step back, then stopped herself, clearly torn between leaving and staying.
"I didn’t mean you are no one," Akane said, the words coming out more rushed now. "I only meant... this is my responsibility. Hitomi is my responsibility. You don’t have to—"
She cut herself off, eyes flickering with frustration and something closer to guilt.
[He’s still looking at me like that. Stop it. Don’t make me feel worse. I already feel bad enough for snapping. For the hug. For everything.]
I stayed silent, waiting, watching the way her clenched hands trembled just slightly at her sides.
Then I looked straight into the eyes behind the mask and spoke quietly, but with clear weight.
"Then what am I supposed to do... if something happens to you? If you get hurt? You’re so selfish for always thinking of yourself. What about me?"
Akane froze.

The words landed harder than any accusation. Her eyes widened behind the black mask, and for a moment she forgot to keep her usual cold composure. Through the lingering telepathic connection, I caught the raw thought that flashed across her mind.
[He is worried about me...]
The realization seemed to shake her more than anything else that had been said. Her fingers, still curled into tight fists at her sides, tightened even further until her knuckles went pale.
I continued, voice steady.
"Just like you are worried about me... I also worry about you. I don’t want you to do anything dangerous."
"Can you promise me that? You always ask me not to use my ability... can you promise me not to do anything dangerous? Then I can also promise you that I won’t use that ability."

chapters.title: Chapter 1257: Giving A Gift To Akane
paragraphs: Akane’s breath caught. The rigid line of her shoulders wavered.

She tried to speak, then stopped. Her gaze dropped for a second before she forced it back up to meet mine, but the usual sharp edge in her eyes had softened into something conflicted and almost fragile.
[He’s asking me to promise... the same way I always ask him. If I refuse, I’m a hypocrite. If I accept... I might not be able to keep it. But the way he’s looking at me right now...]

"I..." she tried again, voice quieter than before. The single word hung in the air between us, unfinished, as the tension in her body warred with the clear guilt and surprise still radiating from her thoughts.
I tilted my head slightly.
"What? Can’t do it?"
Akane lowered her head. The black mask hid most of her expression, but the way her shoulders dropped gave her away.
"...I am sorry for being so selfish."
I stepped forward and pulled her into a tight hug again, one hand resting against the back of her head, the other firm around her waist. This time she didn’t stiffen quite as much.
"You’re not selfish," I said quietly. "You’re just too kind."
While I held her, I accessed theSUDIX System.

The interface unfolded in my mind. I navigated without hesitation, located the Healing Factor ability, and spent eight billion without a second thought. The moment the purchase was confirmed, I initiated the merge and directed the ability straight into Akane.
The transfer was seamless.

Akane’s body jerked almost imperceptibly against me. As a master of physical control, she felt it instantly—an infinite, steady life source flooding through every cell. Hidden micro-damage she hadn’t even been fully aware of began repairing itself.
Old strain from years of missions, residual internal stress, everything quietly mended. And yet the source itself never diminished. It simply remained, vast and constant.
Her eyes widened behind the mask.
"What did you do?"
I kept my expression blank and mildly confused.
"What?"
Her thoughts crashed through the telepathic link, sharp and disbelieving.
[It’s him... he gave it to me. This is his ability. He just... gave me his ability. Why is he treating me like this...?]
Akane’s hands shot up and gripped my shoulders hard. Her voice lost its usual controlled edge.
"Don’t fool me. What did you just do to me?"

She pushed back just enough to look at me properly, fingers still digging into my shoulders. The infinite healing energy continued to circulate inside her body, quiet and inexhaustible. Her breathing had grown uneven.
"This... this power. It’s not temporary. It’s permanent. It’syours. Why would you give me something like this?" Her voice rose slightly.
"Do you have any idea what this means? An ability of this level doesn’t just appear. You transferred it. You gave me your own healing factor."
[He weakened himself. He must have. No one just hands over an ability like this without a cost. What if he needs it later? What if he gets hurt again and can’t recover because of me?]
"Jack." My name came out almost like an accusation. "Take it back. Right now. I didn’t ask for this. I don’t need you to protect me by crippling yourself."
She shook her head once, sharply, the black cloak shifting with the movement.

"You always do this. You throw yourself into danger, you spend things you shouldn’t, and then you act like it’s nothing. What if something happens to you tomorrow? What if you need this exact ability and it’s no longer there because you gave it to me?"
Her grip on my shoulders tightened further.
"I can feel it. It’s endless. It’s still full. That means you didn’t just share a fragment—you moved the entire thing into me. Why? Why would you do something so reckless just because I was worried?"

[He’s looking at me like I’m overreacting. I’m not. He doesn’t understand how dangerous it is for him to keep giving pieces of himself away. First he makes me worry, then he does this. I can’t... I don’t know how to deal with someone who treats their own life so lightly.]
Akane’s voice dropped, but the intensity didn’t.
"Answer me properly. What did it cost you? And don’t you dare say ’nothing.’"
I met her eyes through the mask and answered without flinching.
"You might need it more than me... because I know you won’t listen to me."
The words hit her like a physical blow. Akane’s fingers dug harder into my shoulders. For a second she just stared, the silence between us stretching tight.
Then her voice rose, sharp and angry.
"Who are you to make such a decision for me? Tell me—who are you?"
Her thoughts exploded through the telepathic link, raw and unfiltered.

[Who is he to decide what I need? He just handed over an ability that could keep him alive and acted like it was a casual gift. He doesn’t get to decide that for me. He doesn’t get to decide anything for me.]
She shoved against my chest, not hard enough to break free, but enough to put a small distance between us while still holding onto my shoulders.
"You don’t get to do this. You don’t get to look at me, decide I’m the one who needs protecting, and then strip yourself of something this important. What gives you the right?"
Her breathing had grown faster. The infinite healing factor still hummed quietly inside her body, a constant reminder of what he had just done.

"I am not a child. I am not someone you can just... gift things to when you feel like it. You made this decision without asking me. Without even warning me. And now you’re standing there telling me I need it more than you because I won’t listen?"
[He’s still looking at me with that calm expression. It makes it worse. If he had argued back, it would be easier. Instead he’s just... accepting it. Like my anger doesn’t surprise him at all.]

chapters.title: Chapter 1258: Akane’s Forced Anger
paragraphs: I met her eyes through the mask and spoke quietly.
"I think you deserve it more than me. With this... I don’t have to worry about you getting hurt. It can give me peace of mind, knowing you will not be in any danger."

Akane went completely still. A single tear slipped from the corner of her eye, then another, trailing down beneath the black mask and disappearing into the fabric. More followed, quiet and uncontrolled.
I stepped closer, reached up, and gently wiped the tears that had escaped with my thumb. My voice stayed soft.
"Don’t feel guilty about it, okay? I chose this. You didn’t force anything on me."
Her composure finally cracked. A soft sob broke from her throat. She didn’t push my hand away, but her shoulders trembled once under the black cloak.
"Tell me the truth," she said, voice unsteady. "Why are you so good to me? Just because I am Yuko’s master? Is that the only reason?"
I stayed quiet for a moment, reading the sharp, desperate thought that flashed through her mind.
[I need to know... I need the real answer, not the kind one.]
Then I answered.
"When I found out about you... I knew how good you were to Sister Yuko. Saving her. Teaching her. Giving her a home when she had nowhere else. I just wanted to help you."
I paused, then continued more quietly, holding her gaze through the mask.

"But when I met you... I don’t know how I fell in love with you. I really don’t. It wasn’t planned. I just can’t see you hurt in any way. I feel like I would die if something happened to you. That’s the truth."
Akane froze as if the air had been knocked from her lungs. Her fingers twitched at her sides.
Her thoughts exploded in a chaotic, heartbroken rush that she couldn’t contain.

[He... is confessing to me. He’s actually saying it out loud. What should I do? Reject him immediately? Get angry? Push him away hard enough that he never says it again? He already has a girlfriend... this is cheating. I’m the other woman even if I never asked for it.]

[But if I reject him right now, the look on his face... it will break his heart. I can already see it forming. Why does that hurt me so much? Why does the idea of hurting him make my chest ache like this?]

[Why am I getting flustered like this? My heart is beating too fast. No. I don’t love him. I don’t. I can’t. I don’t even like him... not even a bit. I’m just... surprised. That’s all it is. Surprise.]
I watched her carefully. Her eyes darted away, then back, then away again. A faint flush had risen under the edges of the mask. Her hands, still near my arms, trembled slightly.
Akane’s voice suddenly sharpened with forced anger, though it cracked on the first word.
"What nonsense are you speaking? I am your mother’s age. You haven’t even seen what I look like under this mask... and you already have a girlfriend. Do you hear yourself?"
She took a half-step back, though her body didn’t fully commit to the distance. Her voice rose again, trying to recover control.

"No—it is not a matter of whether you have a girlfriend or not. I don’t like you. Do you understand me? I don’t. If you gave me your ability just because of these... these feelings, then take it back. Right now. I never asked for it."
I let my expression fall, voice soft and deliberately wounded.

"I am sorry... I know I shouldn’t have feelings for you. I know it’s wrong. But I just... can’t control myself. I am sorry for being so disrespectful. I know it puts you in a difficult position, and that was never my intention."
Akane stared at the heartbroken look on my face. Her own heart twisted so painfully that another tear slipped free, then another. Fresh thoughts spilled through the link, rawer than before.

[I love him... damn it, I do love him. I’ve known it for a while, and I’ve been ignoring it every single day. Every time he almost dies, every time he looks at me like I’m the only one who matters, it gets harder to pretend. But he and I can never be together.]
[How will I face Yuko? Her little sister is his girlfriend. If she ever finds out that I... that I stole her sister’s boyfriend... she would never forgive me. I would never forgive myself.]
[Why did he have to say it out loud? Why couldn’t he just keep it to himself? Now I have to hurt him. There’s no other choice. I have to be the one who ends this before it destroys everything.]
"I know you don’t want to see me after this," I continued quietly. "Just accept this ability. This is my heart... for you. And I am sorry, Master Akane. Truly."

She stood there in silence for a long moment, tears still quietly soaking into the edge of her mask. The infinite healing factor hummed steadily inside her body like a second heartbeat she could no longer ignore. When she finally spoke again, her voice was low and strained, almost pleading.

"You can’t just say things like that to me. You can’t look at me with those eyes and expect me to... to simply accept it and stay quiet. I am not someone who can stand beside you openly. I am not someone who should even be having these thoughts in the first place."
Her hands curled into tight fists at her sides. She forced the next words out one by one.

"You already have someone. You have Yuko’s sister. And I... I am the one who is supposed to protect her, not the one who takes what belongs to her. So stop looking at me like that. Stop making me feel like this. Take the ability if you must—keep it, I don’t care—but don’t... don’t give me your heart. I can’t carry it. I don’t know how."
Even as she said the words, her thoughts betrayed her completely.
[I want to carry it. That’s the problem. I want to. And I hate myself for wanting it this much.]
